q: A computable real number x ∈ [0,1] is one for which:
opts: There exists a Turing machine that outputs the n-th binary digit of x for each input n
The binary expansion of x has a period
exp: Computable reals: x is computable if a TM can output any finite approximation to arbitrary precision—equivalently, the sequence of rational approximations is recursively enumerable and converges effectively.
